learning_outcomes.text: Gains the ability to analyze past knowledge using the method of history discipline and produce scientific knowledge.
Acquires knowledge about historiography and schools in the world and Turkey from past to present, recognizes new schools, and evaluates their effects on history.
Develops the skill to identify historical problems, grasps historical events in all aspects, and penetrates them deeply.

Acquires the ability to understand the relationship between current events and processes and the past. Establishes a connection between the singular and the universal through local and oral history research.

Gains the ability to analyze, criticize, and interpret historical texts, becomes proficient in the sources of the subject, and acquires the skill to summarize, transcribe, report, and present in scientific meetings such as communiqués.
Develops reasoning and analytical thinking skills by gaining the ability to approach historical problems academically/objectively.
Gains fundamental knowledge about all periods of history, such as ancient and Islamic history, Turkish history before and after Islam, Ottoman and Republican history, European and World history.
Can use the knowledge and skills acquired in the field of history in studies conducted jointly with other fields of social sciences.
Acquires knowledge about Ottoman, European, and world histories and possesses interpretation, comparison, and analysis skills.
Gains the habit and ability to use libraries and archives, learns the methods of research on a subject, and applies these in other areas of life.

Can analyze specific tools required to work with documents from certain periods, historical texts (such as paleography, epigraphy), inscriptions, and epitaphs, and acquires knowledge and skill in using source texts in various languages.
Embraces the importance of lifelong learning, follows developments on scientific and contemporary topics, and improves oneself; acquires scientific ethical and responsibility consciousness.

Acquires knowledge and skill in using information access tools such as bibliographic repertoires, archival inventories, and electronic references. Gains the ability to create, organize, transmit, store, present, and share information in the field of history using information and internet technologies.
Acquires individual study skills and the ability to make independent decisions, expressing ideas and criticisms constructively, verbally, and in writing, clearly and concisely.

assessment_rules: Midterm and final exam dates are not specified in the 14-week course plan. Midterm and final exam dates are held on the dates specified in the academic calendar by the decision of our University Senate.
